Given how this article already has a pretty solid link to SCP-643 builtin via the addendum, I'm tempted to simply add a link to Site-77's dossier and move on. However, there is room for an additional sentence at the end of that same addendum that can serve as a means of linking SCP-703 to a few more articles by virtue of those articles being located at Site-77, namely SCP-649 and SCP-1317. As such, I am proposing the following edit:

Changing the following:

On 9/18/2010, several instances of SCP-643 suddenly vanished from their containment chamber. During the ensuing lockdown by security personnel, SCP-703 entered its active phase, and produced the missing instances. Due to SCP-643's mind affecting properties, three researchers were injured and one member of security was killed before they could be recontained. Because of the fact that SCP-643 was being moved to a containment chamber in the same zone as SCP-703, it is theorized that SCP-703 was attempting to assist in this move. Reclassification to Euclid has been granted, and SCP-703 has been moved to a more secure area.

To this:

On 9/18/2010, several instances of SCP-643 suddenly vanished from their containment chamber. During the ensuing lockdown by security personnel, SCP-703 entered its active phase, and produced the missing instances. Due to SCP-643's mind affecting properties, three researchers were injured and one member of security was killed before they could be recontained. Because of the fact that SCP-643 was being moved to a containment chamber in the same zone as SCP-703, it is theorized that SCP-703 was attempting to assist in this move. Reclassification to Euclid has been granted, and SCP-703 has been moved to a more secure area. As of the time of writing, similar incidents have been observed with instances of SCP-649 and SCP-1317.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: From Brucy
item.content:encoded:
Heya guys, very long time no see. For those of you who don't know, I am the origional writer of this article, back when it was just SCP-703 The Random Item Generator. Agent Brucy, at yer service.

Anyway, I had some down time, of which these past few years I have had very little. We're talking a few fleeting moments of sleep a night busy here. It has been so long that it took a good half an hour of scanning to even find the page. All I could remember was that it was Seven-Oh-Something.

Needless to say, I had to pick my best guess and found it right out.

At first, I was angry, dispirited, and rather irate. Had I found out the article had been changed when I was but a fledgling boy, I would probably be pounding the keyboard with ape-like bravado. All writers like myself (The kind that aren't very good, know it, but still like to pretend that they're the next Hemmingway.) definately take all serious rewrites to their work as a massive slap in the face.

Instead, I opt to take it with a grain of salt, which, it is said, helps all poisons go down a little easier.

Drivle, like what I had posted origionally, never needs an explenation, but always recieves the most. Ask any Elitest art-snub what makes fecal-smeared canvas so special and they will launch into a tirade that could make a Keter Class SCP cower in fear.

I was going off of an idea that I had while contemplating the deeper mysteries of human nature and morality (Like all semi-macabre 16-17 year-olds are wont to do) and decided that a propperly inhuman SCP should have no rhyme nor reason in its dealings. I attempted to write an SCP that couldn't be reasoned to have a human, demi-human, semi-human, quasi-human, or proto-human Modus Operandi. Every item that came out of it was intended to be nonsensical, because nonsense is terrifying to a kid's uncertain world durring a time when personal moral upheaval is the name of the game.

It didn't come out good. In fact, if it had been left alone, I probably would have smacked myself when I found it for ever having been as tired and hackneyed as I was when I was younger.

So, instead I wanna say thanks, from the bottom of my heart, for turning a cruddy, hopeless article around and ensuring that my ideas are still present, even if just the framework.
yaaaay

I see what you're saying, but we have a number of things that work on the "anglerfish" principle, and really there's nothing wrong with things on this site being heartwarming or amusing (Pesterbot, for example, doesn't need to secretly drive you crazy and make you suddenly start calling yourself Prime Minister Sinistar or something to be a good article). Not to mention I look at your description, and immediately get the feeling that we basically -have- that SCP already written up…

As for why we don't let people in, I was about to ask the same question when I hit on a possibility. Imagine if we allowed a researcher to go in there and pick something up. The closet picks up on there being such a person in there, and produces the SCP object he currently happens to be working on.

Now imagine that said object is 106. Or 682. Or Abel. Or hell, maybe it's 447-2 and a dead body. The road to XK-class is paved with just wanting to help…

item.content:encoded:
Picture this: The sun is setting. Bedtime is close. A little girls room is cast in long shadows and orange light from her window. She's playing in the floor with her blocks, not minding anything. A single light bulb, hanging within the otherwise pitch black closet, flickers and comes on. A doll is sitting in it, slumped over. The girl notices. "Lucy! Momma said you was gone!" She gets up from her blocks, and hurries to the closet. Walks inside, kneels down, touches the doll.

The light bulb goes out …
(Not great writing, but a decent example)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I see a lot of people thought the addendum strengthened the SCP. I have to say, I found it a let down. Its helpful and sympathetic, which is fine, but my mind was going in a completely different direction.

A closet that magically acquires something that its audience desires, combined with the fact only D class are allowed to retrieve them… Why the restriction? Can the closet harm someone inside it? To me the logical conclusion wasn't that the closet was being helpful, but that it was acquiring bait. It has toys and snacks to lure in kids, and when there are no kids, it's bait changes to something that would entice the foundation staff. It WANTS you to step inside for the prize, like a snapping turtle. I was honestly shocked when it didn't turn out to be a malevolent monster-in-the-closet. Read the article again, with this sort of explanation in mind, and its surprisingly chilling. Not saying it needs any sort of revision, just my experience.
